What is PrismaShift and what is it like to use?

Long image

A

Answer

PrismaShift is a self-hosted photo sorter for a home server. A customer drops images on a web page. Each one is filed into a folder by what kind of image it is: camera photo, screenshot, tall, wide or square. An admin can review the log and undo any move from the command line.

  1. The web upload path works today: we uploaded five images and each was sorted and listed in the gallery within seconds.1
  2. Sorting uses fixed rules on the file name, camera tags and shape, not a trained model.2
  3. Every move is written to a SQLite log, so rollback can put a file back where it came from.3
  4. It is an early prototype (v0.1.0, one commit): the folder watcher is not switched on, and the Docker setup does not start as shipped.

Applies toRepo NoJuanNobody/prismashift at commit b5229f9run locally with Python 3.12 on 2026-10-20the Docker image was run with the compose mounts, but not with Docker Compose itself

1

What does a customer and an admin do, step by step?

Diagram structure
  • Open dashboard open
  • Drop images drop
  • See gallery, get ZIP gallery
  • Read file and tags classify
  • Move into folder route
  • Write to log log
  • Check history history
  • Roll back a move undo
  • classify → route · category
  • drop → classify · upload
  • history → undo · if wrong
  • log → history
  • open → drop
  • route → gallery · sorted
  • route → log
  1. Open dashboard ↗

    The admin starts the server; the customer opens it in a browser (port 8080 in the README).

  2. Drop images ↗

    Drag files onto the drop zone or browse. JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC and AVIF are accepted.

  3. Read file and tags ↗

    The server checks the file name, camera make and model, and width against height. The first rule that matches wins.

  4. Move into folder ↗

    The file moves into a folder named after its category. A short random suffix keeps names unique.

  5. Write to log ↗

    Each move is stored with its old path, new path, SHA-256 hash and rule.

  6. See gallery, get ZIP ↗

    The upload row turns green or blue with "Routed to Type A" or "Type B", and the gallery and activity list refresh.

  7. Check history ↗

    prismashift-admin history lists recent moves with IDs.

  8. Roll back a move ↗

    prismashift-admin rollback <id> moves the file back to where it came from.

2

What goes in and what comes out?

These are real results from prismashift-admin test-rules on five test images we made.

Image droppedRule that matchedFolderDashboard group
IMG_2041.jpg (4032×3024, camera tag Canon)camera tag present, 90%photos/Type A
Screenshot 2026-10-12 at 09.14.png"screenshot" in file name, 95%screenshots/Type B
mountain_pano.jpg (3000×1500)wider than tall, 85%landscape/Type A
beach_walk.jpg (1200×1800)taller than wide, 85%portrait/Type B
logo_draft.png (1080×1080)about square, 85%square/Type B

The percentages are fixed numbers that the code sets for each rule.2 Because the shape rule always matches a readable image, the high-res and low-res rules never run, and only unreadable files land in unclassified/.

3

What does the admin see?

The admin tool is a terminal command with six subcommands: status, scan, test-rules, history, rollback and reprocess.4 scan --dry-run and test-rules preview results without moving files.

A batch scan prints one batch ID, and rollback <batch-id> undoes the whole batch. Dashboard uploads go one file per request, so each upload gets its own batch ID.

4

First open shows sample cards

Until the first real upload, the gallery shows built-in sample cards with stock photos, and labels such as "Neural Classifier" and "S3 Sync" are fixed page text. The counters switch to real numbers once the server answers.
